A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REVERSE study. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including relocated material and v3's added checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original REVERSE benchmark evaluations, component ablations, threshold and temperature studies, and bootstrap results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds efficiency, POPE subset, general VQA and caption-quality evaluations.

M1.justification: The confidence tokens, masked training loss, hierarchical backtracking, rejection sampling and query rewriting remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Expanded data-curation explanations do not establish a revised method; the altered stopping rule is confined to the new efficiency experiment.

E1.justification: Table A.3 adds evaluation on HallusionBench, GQA and MM-Vet. This substantially broadens evaluation to general VQA capability preservation and visually misleading inputs. The original training-data coverage and hallucination benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the retained benchmark tables and analyses. The additional evaluations reuse the existing LLaVA-v1.5-7B reference. FAVA is discussed for positioning, while CLAIR is introduced as a metric.

E3.justification: The new efficiency experiment varies correction budgets from 0 to 50, continues generation after exhausting the budget, and measures generated-token ratios. v3 also adds CLAIR evaluation and specifies tau=0.5 for the new VQA comparisons. Table A.2 labels POPE scores as accuracy although the retained protocol specifies F1; this inconsistency does not establish a reliable metric replacement.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends analysis with correction-budget versus token-cost measurements, Popular/Adversarial/Random POPE breakdowns, and explicit checks of general VQA and caption-quality preservation. Existing component, threshold and temperature analyses remain. Earlier diagnostics about skipped cases and the absence of harmful corrections are removed from the efficiency discussion.

E5.justification: The 100-round bootstrap procedure and existing REVERSE confidence intervals are retained. Table A.2 newly reports confidence intervals for the LLaVA baseline, including its pooled POPE estimate of 85.9 with interval 83.2-88.2. No increased run count or new seed information is reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new result sets are added, while Tables 1-4 and the matched bootstrap tables retain their values. Table 5 reports CHAIR from 7.8 to 6.0 and token ratios from 1.00x to 3.05x across correction budgets. Newly reported REVERSE/base scores are 45.44/46.94 on HallusionBench, 62.73/62.00 on GQA, 28.40/31.10 on MM-Vet, and 0.7264/0.7384 on CLAIR. POPE subset results are also added.

T1.justification: The training-loss equation and metric definitions in Equations A.2-A.5 are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical proofs or theorems; the expanded efficiency discussion supplies informal cost reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion retain the unified self-verification framework, 1.3M-sample dataset, and claimed improvements of up to 12% on CHAIR-MSCOCO and 34% on HaloQuest. Added introductory emphasis on controllability restates capabilities already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: v3 separates verification and correction costs and explicitly acknowledges additional generated tokens. It newly interprets the supplementary scores as preserving general capabilities and caption quality, and distinguishes HallusionBench's visually misleading inputs from the targeted hallucinations. Most dataset-bias and discriminative-task limitations are relocated from Appendix C to Section 5.

D1.justification: Appendix B expands documentation of negative-example generation and quality control, while omitting earlier explicit statements about answer-only annotation and tag validation. Training recipes, hardware and release links remain unchanged. Its new GPT-4o wording conflicts with the retained GPT-4o-mini description, so an actual generator change cannot be established.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to CLAIR and FAVA. Appendix B newly positions REVERSE's dataset against FAVA through stated differences in scale and hallucination diversity, including 1.3M versus 35K samples. The main related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, Section 4.2 and Appendix B. The efficiency discussion is reordered, limitations move into the main text, and a NeurIPS checklist and conference footer are added. Most scientific exposition retains its structure and wording.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5 and Tables A.2-A.4, compresses and places Table 4 beside Table 5, and reflows the existing bootstrap tables as A.5-A.7. Existing figures retain their content; the appendix qualitative figure and algorithm move onto separate pages. These are localized display changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's largely qualitative efficiency assurances, Table 5 makes computational trade-offs inspectable, and the added VQA and CLAIR evaluations improve empirical transparency. The gains are limited: efficiency uses token counts under a modified stopping rule, and mixed VQA/CLAIR scores do not firmly establish blanket capability preservation. These additions modestly strengthen the paper without changing its central method or headline evidence.
